extracted.intended_audience: peer reviewers (and prospective reviewers) for PLOS Global Public Health
extracted.subtask_short: PLOS Global Public Health peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for reviewers evaluating manuscripts submitted to PLOS Global Public Health, emphasising technical rigor, ethical standards, reporting and reproducibility, plus procedural expectations for submitting reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accept invitation only if qualified and available
rubrics_metrics.description: Accept an invitation only if you have the knowledge, time and objectivity necessary to provide an unbiased assessment of the research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer invitations are sent via Editorial Manager; use links to accept/decline. In agreeing to complete a review you also give permission to publish your review under a Creative Commons Attribution CC BY license.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review model options
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS Global Public Health practices single-anonymized peer review by default, but offers signed and published peer review options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Single-anonymized: reviewer knows authors but name not shared; review appears in editorial decision letter read by authors and other reviewers. Signed: reviewer may choose to sign and authors/other reviewers will see the name. Published peer review history: if authors publish peer review history, the editorial decision letter including the review will appear alongside the article; reviewer name appears only if signed. Reviews may be portable to other PLOS journals if authors transfer manuscript.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: A competing interest is anything that interferes with or could be perceived as potentially interfering with a thorough and objective assessment of a manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Common examples: recent or current collaboration with any of the authors; direct competition or history of scientific conflict with any authors; opportunity to profit financially from the work. Do not accept a review assignment if you have a competing interest or don’t feel able to give an objective assessment. If unsure, contact the journal. If asked to review despite a competing interest, declare it when you submit your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit collaborators / disclose co-reviewing
rubrics_metrics.description: If you had help completing the review you must share your collaborator’s name with the journal when you submit the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enter collaborator’s name in question 2 under 'Confidential comments to Editor' or via email. Do not include collaborator’s name in the text of the review itself. Competing interests and confidentiality policies apply to all reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep manuscripts and correspondence confidential and do not share information about submissions unless previously agreed with the editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should not make use of material or take advantage of any information gained through the peer review process. Read the PLOS Confidentiality Policy for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat previous reviews as not definitive
rubrics_metrics.description: If you reviewed the article at another journal, consider the manuscript as a new submission unless instructed otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep in mind the manuscript may have been revised; PLOS Global Public Health's criteria may differ from other journals. Inform the editor if you reviewed a previous version at another journal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeframe for review
rubrics_metrics.description: Aim to complete your review within 10 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you need more time, email the journal as soon as possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: ORCID reviewer credit (optional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Link your PLOS reviewer account to your ORCID record to receive reviewer activity credit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set up syncing to have reviewer activity automatically posted to your ORCID profile; this records completion of a review but won’t publish the content of your review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of the structured reviewer form
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS uses a structured reviewer form to focus reviewers on publication criteria and improve review efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form has two sections: 'Comments to the author' (questions 1-4 required dropdowns such as Yes/No/I don't know/N/A; question 5 is 'Review Comments to the Author' where you enter the main text) and 'Comments to the editor' (declare competing interests, list collaborators, indicate if submission should be highlighted). Answers in 'Comments to the author' are included in the decision letter to the author.

rubrics_metrics.name: No confidential comments except competing interests
rubrics_metrics.description: PLOS Global Public Health does not allow confidential comments other than the declaration of competing interests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have confidential concerns relating to publication or research ethics, contact the journal office directly at the provided email; do not put confidential ethics concerns in the confidential comments field beyond competing interests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enter reviews in submission system
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviews must be entered in the Editorial Manager submission system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email the journal office if you have trouble accessing the manuscript or entering comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original research requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The study presents the results of original research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is one of seven editorial criteria that must be satisfied for acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: No prior publication of results
rubrics_metrics.description: Results reported have not been published elsewhere.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS expects submissions to be original and not previously published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical quality and methodological detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Experiments, statistics, and other analyses are performed to a high technical standard and are described in sufficient detail.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should assess technical rigour, appropriateness of statistical analyses, and whether methods are described sufficiently for evaluation and reproduction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions supported by data
rubrics_metrics.description: Conclusions are presented in an appropriate fashion and are supported by the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that claims are proportionate to evidence and that interpretations do not overreach the data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and standard English
rubrics_metrics.description: The article is presented in an intelligible fashion and is written in standard English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess readability and organization; determine if manuscript is accessible to intended readership and non-specialists when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ethics and research integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: The research meets all applicable standards for the ethics of experimentation and research integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirm appropriate ethical approvals, consent, and integrity standards have been met; raise concerns to editors if not.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to reporting and data availability standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The article adheres to appropriate reporting guidelines and community standards for data availability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check conformity to relevant guidelines (e.g., CONSORT, MIAME, QUORUM, STROBE, Fort Lauderdale agreement) and that data availability statements and repository accessions are provided where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify and evaluate main claims and significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine the main claims of the paper and how significant they are for the discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess novelty and contribution to the field; indicate if claims are important, incremental, or negligible and why.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement in literature and fairness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the claims are properly placed in the context of the previous literature and whether the authors have treated the literature fairly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note missing citations, biased representation of prior work, or failure to acknowledge competing findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data and analyses must fully support claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the data and analyses fully support the claims, and if not, what other evidence is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify additional analyses, controls, or data needed to bolster claims; be explicit about gaps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protocol adherence and deviations
rubrics_metrics.description: If a protocol is provided, check for important deviations and whether authors have explained why deviations occurred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For trials or prespecified protocols, flag unexplained deviations and request justification or additional reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommend supporting information for methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend that detailed protocols and algorithms be published as supporting information online when warranted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate if particular methods warrant extensive protocols or algorithm sharing as supplemental material to aid reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assess potential for resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: If the paper is unsuitable in its present form, judge whether the study shows sufficient potential that the authors should be encouraged to resubmit a revised version.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide constructive guidance on what would be required to make the manuscript acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data deposition and accession reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Original data should be deposited in appropriate repositories and accession/version numbers provided for genes, proteins, mutants, diseases, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify that repository links, accession numbers, or data availability statements are present and usable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conform to relevant reporting guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the study conforms to relevant guidelines such as CONSORT, MIAME, QUORUM, STROBE, and the Fort Lauderdale agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Request completion of checklists or adherence statements where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methodological detail sufficient for reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Details of the methodology should be sufficient to allow the experiments to be reproduced.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Flag missing procedural details, reagent/source information, sample size calculations, and analytic code; request additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Software availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Is any software created by the authors freely available?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage open-source or publicly available software; request links or code repositories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility to non-specialists
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the manuscript well organized and written clearly enough to be accessible to non-specialists?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess clarity of background, explanation of technical terms, and organization for broader readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review revised manuscripts and author responses
rubrics_metrics.description: Original reviewers are often asked to evaluate revised manuscripts and the authors’ responses to reviewer comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make yourself available for re-review and follow-up questions from editors where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not edit or delete reviewer reports (editorial handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Editorial Board members should not edit or delete reviewer reports and should notify PLOS staff before sending a decision letter if they have concerns about a reviewer’s comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PLOS staff will not change reviewer comments intended for authors except where language is inappropriate for professional communication or comments contain confidential information or would incur a major risk if conveyed. In other cases staff/handling editors may advise authors they can disregard a reviewer’s comments in whole or part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial decision process
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors make the final decision on whether to publish each submission based on reviewers’ comments, the PLOS Global Public Health criteria for publication, and their own assessment of the manuscript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers’ recommendations are considered but editors weigh reviews alongside authors’ responses and other material; final decisions are not mechanical majority votes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling conflicting reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: If reviewers disagree fundamentally, editors may share all reviews with reviewers and request additional comments to help reach a decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions are not necessarily made by majority rule; editors may solicit extra input, consult additional experts, or use discretion based on the merits of arguments presented.
